key_insight: The paper introduces a Turing-test style, human-centered evaluation framework that systematically measures whether video foundation models used as embodied world models are perceptually indistinguishable from reality and robust under realistic disturbances. It exposes gaps between model generative quality and what human observers accept for downstream embodied tasks.
problem_solved: Lack of a comprehensive, standardized evaluation to judge whether video-based world models (1) maintain perceptual fidelity to human observers and (2) remain robust across realistic embodied scenarios and perturbations before being used in downstream tasks.
method: Design a human-centered ‘Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test’ where human judges compare real vs. model-generated video predictions across diverse embodied scenarios.
Assemble a benchmark suite of embodied tasks, controlled perturbations, and failure modes to probe robustness (e.g., occlusion, viewpoint shifts, interaction dynamics).
Combine human preference data with automated perceptual and task-relevant metrics to produce a composite, interpretable score for model readiness.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, interpretable evaluation pipeline to decide whether video foundation models are visually and behaviorally reliable for embodied downstream tasks, accelerating safer deployment and targeted model improvements.

paper_title: Wow, wo, val! A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test
paper_authors: Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaozhu Ju, Hao Li, Yong Bao
